## Fix opencode tool-override breakage and add a permanent parse guard. — 2026-08-01 (parent afcad82163ab)

**Fixed a JS unterminated-string bug in all 19 opencode tool-override templates and added a hermetic parse guard to prevent recurrence.**

All 19 `_render_opencode_*` functions in `trie/tool_override_install` had `.join("\n")` rendered with a single-backslash `\n`, which placed a literal newline inside a JS string literal and caused opencode to fail loading the entire tools directory. The backslash is now escaped to `\\n` so the generated TypeScript receives the intended escape sequence.

To prevent this class of bug from shipping again, three new test symbols were added to `tests/test_tool_override_install`:

- `_REGEX_START_CHARS` — punctuation set identifying positions where `/` begins a regex rather than a division operator.
- `_first_raw_newline_in_quoted_string` — pure-Python JS/TS lexer that detects a raw newline inside `'`/`"`-quoted strings, descending into `${}` template interpolations and skipping comments and regex literals.
- `_rendered_opencode_ts_files` — shared fixture that renders all opencode `.ts` overrides keyed by filename.
- `test_rendered_ts_overrides_have_no_unterminated_string_literals` — hermetic regression guard using the scanner above; runs everywhere with no JS runtime.
- `test_scanner_flags_a_known_unterminated_string_literal` — validates the scanner against known-good and known-bad inputs.
- `test_rendered_ts_overrides_parse_under_js_runtime` — opportunistic `bun build` parse check, skipped when `bun` is absent.
